thread:
anya: quick heads-up — i've been prototyping a fallback sampling policy for exporter backpressure. idea: when exporter queue length or send latency crosses a threshold, demote head sampling for low-tier routes, keep tail sampling for errors and slow requests. want feedback before i wire this into the console rollout UI.

matt: can you sketch the exact trigger signals? exporter queue in #msgs or ms? also worried about losing visibility for regressions if we naively drop head. :thinking:

anya: thanks — current plan uses two signals: exporter_queue_count > 5k OR exporter_avg_send_ms > 250ms over 1m window. fallback does: set head_rate -> 0.01 for low tiers, keep head_rate 1.0 for high tiers, and always keep tail sampling on spans with status != OK.

li: +1 to the triggers but we need to be careful with tenant fairness. if a single tenant floods, does fallback affect only that tenant's routes or whole exporter? we should scope by route/tenant.

anya: scoped per-route and per-tenant. global fallback only if exporter-level health is degraded AND >50% of traffic is from top 3 tenants — to avoid noisy neighbors causing platform-wide visibility loss.

matt: i still want a small continuous probe so we can detect regressions in low-tier routes. propose keeping a random 0.1% head sample across all routes even during fallback, plus preserving the last-k spans per trace for tail.

zach: from console/rollout UX POV we should expose: estimated stored-spans delta, sample coverage % by route, and an opt-out override per-tenant. PMs will ask for numbers not just toggles.

anya: agreed. here's a draft of the route config we'd expose via the API (proto-yaml):
```
routes:
  - name: api.v1.chat
    tier: low
    sampling:
      fallback:
        triggers:
          exporter_queue_count: 5000
          exporter_avg_send_ms: 250
        actions:
          head_rate: 0.01
          keep_tail_errors: true
          preserve_probe_rate: 0.001  # 0.1% global probe
```

li: that looks ok. what about retention interplay? if we drop head from 100%->1% for low-tier, stored-spans will drop a lot. need the console to show projected retention cost delta (30/90 day).

matt: also: add metric sample_coverage_by_route (rolling 1h) and alert if coverage < probe_rate * 0.5 for > 6h. that'll surface misconfig or rollout mistakes.

telemetry-bot: exporter-stats: exporter-a queue=6400 avg_send_ms=310 dropped_batches=12 in last 60s — suggest entering fallback mode for routes: api.v1.chat, api.v1.search

anya: perfect — telemetry-bot confirms the proto. i'll gate the rollout under a canary slider in the console (0%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) and include per-tenant overrides and a preview of estimated daily stored spans. zach — can you mock the UI preview numbers?

zach: i'll mock as soon as you share the mapping from head_rate -> estimated spans/day by route. will add a confidence band and a small tooltip: "probe preserves visibility for regressions".

li: i'll run a stress job against exporter-a and validate scoping works as expected. ping me when you have the canary flag.

anya: thanks all. action items: anya add probe rate and sample_coverage metric to the rollout proto; matt add alert rule; zach mock console preview; li run exporter stress test. i'll open a PR + staging rollout tomorrow. :thumbsup:

matt: noted. if we land, let's include an eval-run that measures model-level latency regressions vs sample coverage.

zach: :white_check_mark:

li: will post results in this thread.

telemetry-bot: note: scheduled export backlog check runs every 15s. current state saved to /var/telemetry/backlog-stats.json

anya: moving to implement — tagging the PR with "telemetry/fallback-sampler". feel free to DM if you want early access to the staging rollout.
